title: Flat-fee uptime bundles and escrowed upgrade schedule for Private/VPC
creator: Asha Menon
description:
Goal: validate a flat-fee packaging model for Private/VPC customers that bundles a license fee, support tier, and a clearly escrowed upgrade cadence to reduce negotiation friction and simplify procurement. Scope: define 3 bundle tiers (Core, Resilient, Mission-Critical) with uptime SLA bands, emergency patch SLAs, quarterly vs. monthly upgrade windows, and an optional escrowed upgrade schedule for regulated customers that require strictly defined maintenance/upgrade windows and rollback guarantees.

Key trade-offs considered: cost transparency vs. revenue upside (flat fee limits per-unit price capture); stricter escrow/upgrade guarantees increase legal and engineering risk and require running extended compatibility testing; longer upgrade cadences reduce ops burden but increase security/compatibility surface. We propose mitigations: staged canary windows, documented rollback playbooks, and an "upgrade escrow" contract addendum that puts a certified image and upgrade plan under escrow with a mutually agreed maintenance SLA.

Pricing experiment approach: 1) Anchor price bands by expected committed GPU-hours and historical token throughput from pilot accounts; 2) Run two-week procurement pilots with 6 pilot customers across finance/healthcare/fintech to collect willingness-to-pay and security questionnaire bottlenecks; 3) Offer optional add-ons (KMS/HSM integration, extended log retention, annual on-site runbooks) priced as modular line items.

Operational requirements: legal to draft the escrow addendum and SOW language; security to sign off on KMS/HSM and data-residency references for the SQ response templates; engineering to produce an upgrade compatibility matrix and a validated rollback procedure; finance to model ARR impact and revenue recognition for flat-fee contracts.

Acceptance criteria: 1) Complete pricing matrix and customer-facing bundle page copy; 2) Draft escrow addendum and SOW templates reviewed by Legal & Security; 3) Two pilot customers signed with agreed SLAs and telemetry enabled to measure true uptime and maintenance window adherence; 4) Internal runbook + rollback checklist merged into private-infra repo and referenced in the SOW; 5) Evidence from pilots of willingness-to-pay or an actionable counter-proposal.

Success metrics: conversion rate from pilot to paid contract >= 40%; average contract ARR >= $150k for Mission-Critical tier; mean time to rollback < 60 minutes in canary windows; fewer than 2 escalations per customer per quarter for upgrade-related incidents.

2026-02-18 - Eng deep-dive: estimated 6 engineer-weeks to build compatibility matrix and automated smoke tests for upgrade windows. Proposed phased delivery: canary tools (2w), rollback tooling (2w), certification harness (2w).
2026-02-25 - Pricing workshop: finance proposed two anchors per tier and a usage-topup model. Decision: pilot will test strictly flat-fee with an optional usage top-up to avoid early overcommitment.

2026-03-02 - Design review: created initial customer offer page mockups. Feedback: surface upgrade cadence prominently and include a \"what happens during an upgrade\" modal. Link to mock: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake/link-design-mock

2026-03-05 - Security questionnaire prep: drafted SQ responses for the package and flagged unanswered questions around HSM key rotation. Action: Security to prepare standard HSM rotation clause before pilot onboarding.
2026-03-09 - Sales/AE feedback: OKRs from two pilot customers indicate procurement prefers flat-fee but asks for an annual true-up clause. Added to acceptance criteria as optional negotiation path.
2026-03-12 - Internal review: Legal and Security provided redlines on escrow addendum. Awaiting final Legal sign-off before pilot contracts are executed.
